In general, if we have a polynomial $$ f(x) = a_nx^n+a_{n-1}x^{n-1}+...+a_{1}x + a_0 $$ with leading coefficient $a_n\neq 0,$ the end behavior of the polynomial is always $$ f(x) \rightarrow +\infty \quad \text{or} \quad f(x) \rightarrow -\infty $$ as $x \rightarrow \pm \infty.$ The sign of infinity depends on whether the leading exponent is even or odd, and on the sign of the leading coefficient. - If the leading coefficient is *positive*, then $f(x) \to +\infty$ as $x \to +\infty.$ Otherwise, if the leading coefficient is *negative*, then $f(x) \to -\infty$ as $x \to +\infty.$ - If the leading exponent is *even*, then the end behavior as $x \to +\infty$ is the *same* as the end behavior as $x \to -\infty.$ Otherwise, if the leading exponent is *odd*, then the end behavior as $x \to +\infty$ is *opposite* the end behavior as $x \to -\infty.$ The different cases are summarized in the table below.
$n$ $a_n$ $x \rightarrow -\infty$ $x \rightarrow +\infty$ Sketch
Even $>0$ $f(x) \rightarrow +\infty$ $f(x) \rightarrow +\infty$
$<0$ $f(x) \rightarrow -\infty$ $f(x) \rightarrow -\infty$
Odd $>0$ $f(x) \rightarrow -\infty$ $f(x) \rightarrow +\infty$
$<0$ $f(x) \rightarrow +\infty$ $f(x) \rightarrow -\infty$

We see that the value of the digit $2$ in the thousandths place is $100$ times *smaller* than the value of the digit $2$ in the tenths place, because: $$ \underbrace{10\times 10}_{2\,\text{steps}}=100 $$ This is the same as saying that the size of the digit $2$ in the thousandths place is $\frac{1}{100}$ the size of the digit $2$ in the tenths place.
